literal: Upon smelling will wither the aniccam; face having changed upon looking will wither the guest.
translation: The delicate aniccam flower withers just by being smelled. A guest withers when looked at with a changed face.
modern: மோந்து பார்த்தாலே அனிச்ச மலர் வாடிவிடும். அதுபோல, முகம் சுளித்து வேறுபட்டுப் பார்த்தாலே வந்த விருந்தினர் உள்ளம் வாடிவிடுவார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet illustrates the extreme sensitivity of guests by comparing them to the delicate aniccam flower. The flower droops simply from the breath of someone smelling it. Similarly, a guest's heart will wither the moment a host looks at them with a changed or unwelcoming expression. The parallel between smelling and looking emphasizes that even the slightest hint of displeasure is enough to hurt a guest, highlighting the need for a genuinely cheerful welcome.
